editorial.headline: Household Rental, Nationally Open but Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A wide rental category for household and personal goods, open nationally to full foreign ownership but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Personal and household rental is often mistaken for a narrow shopfront business. This activity is broader: it covers the rental and operational leasing, without an option to buy, of personal and household goods not otherwise specified within its stated scope. The practical inventory can include textiles, ready-made clothing and footwear—curtains and shoes are named examples—alongside jewellery, household furniture, pottery and glassware, kitchen equipment and electrical appliances. Recreational and sports equipment sit outside the stated activity. It also reaches the rental of ornamental fish with aquariums, where care and cleaning services may accompany the aquarium.

That breadth matters because the registration is framed by the activity being carried on, not by a single product line. A provider whose offer moves between home furnishings, kitchen items and personal goods can still be understood through this defined rental-and-operational-leasing scope, provided the goods remain within it and the arrangement has no purchase option. The activity is open at every listed business scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. This gives the category a broad operating frame, from a focused rental inventory to a larger service handling many kinds of eligible goods, including the distinctive aquarium-and-ornamental-fish offering.

At the national level, the ownership reading is straightforward. The record marks the activity as open to foreign investment and sets the maximum foreign ownership at 100%. In national terms, foreign ownership may therefore reach the full 100% ceiling. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. This is the national investment position for the activity, and it must be read separately from the provincial registration position in Bali.

Bali changes the immediate answer. A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today: the Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO, and the record marks it blocked for PMA registration. The reason is not a Bali-specific ownership percentage. Rather, the OSS risk at the Large scale is Low or Medium-Low across every scope, bringing the activity within Bali’s moratorium. The provincial rule is island-wide and permanent for this risk classification; the record dates the cited moratorium to May 2026. Nationally, foreign ownership can reach 100%, but Bali’s moratorium prevents PMA registration today.
